title: Finite exceptional translations of monotone diagram regions on coordinate faces
statement:
Let $n\ge1$. Identify $\mathbf N^n$ with the exponent vectors of monomials $Y^\alpha$ in $\mathbf Z[Y_1,\ldots,Y_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $D\subseteq\mathbf N^n$ be closed under addition by $\mathbf N^n$. Suppose that $\alpha-\alpha_p e_p+\alpha_p e_t\in D$ for every $\alpha\in D$ and $1\le p<t\le n$, where $e_j$ is the $j$th coordinate vector. Let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_s$ be the finite list of coordinatewise minimal elements of $D$, ordered lexicographically by $(|\alpha|,\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)$, where $|\alpha|=\sum_j\alpha_j$. Set
$$\Delta_i=\{\beta\in\mathbf N^n:\alpha_i+\beta\notin\bigcup_{h<i}(\alpha_h+\mathbf N^n)\},\qquad \Delta_0=\mathbf N^n\setminus D,$$
and $M=\max(\{1\}\cup\{|\alpha_i|:1\le i\le s\})$. For $0\le r<n$ put $F_r=\{\beta:\beta_1=\cdots=\beta_r=0\}$. For every $i=0,\ldots,s$ the exceptional set
$$E_{i,r}=\{\beta\in\Delta_i\cap F_r:\beta+e_{r+1}\notin\Delta_i\}$$
is contained in $\{\beta\in F_r:\beta_j<M\text{ for every }j>r\}$, and is therefore finite. The conventions include $D=\varnothing$ (no vertices) and $D=\mathbf N^n$ (the single vertex $0$).

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11 and 2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, for the parent route. Agent quantitative refinement of Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Lemma 8.2 and Remarks 8.4, pp.274--275: the disjoint vertex regions and the complementary monomials have finite exceptional translations on coordinate faces. Read online at https://mahalex.net/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf. No Stacks tag states this exponent-diagram combinatorial result; journal paper absent from repository literature.

proof.text: Since $0\le r<n$, $k=r+1$ satisfies $1\le k\le n$, and $j>r$ is equivalent to $j\ge k$ for an integer coordinate index $j$. Put $U_q=\bigcup_{h\le q}(\alpha_h+\mathbf N^n)$. The assumed list enumerates exactly the coordinatewise minimal elements of $D$, in the strict ascending degree-lex order required by [lem-trf-monotone-vertex-prefix]. The hypotheses on $D$ are precisely its additive closure and whole-coordinate moves. Therefore $U_s=D$ and each $U_q$ has both closure properties, including $U_0=\varnothing$. No existence of a finite vertex list is inferred: it is a hypothesis. By definition $M\ge1$ and every listed generator has total degree at most $M$. In particular the earlier set used for vertex $i$ is the index prefix $U_{i-1}$, even when several vertices have the same degree.

source.place: Agent coordinate proof of the quantitative exceptional-box refinement; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 (printed pp.93--94) gives only the parent resolution route. Compare Bierstone--Milman 1997, section 8, pp.273--275 (read online; absent from repository literature).

proof.text: For $i\ge1$ and $\beta\in E_{i,r}$, set $v=\alpha_i+\beta$. The definition of $\Delta_i$ gives $\beta\in\Delta_i\iff v\notin U_{i-1}$ and $\beta+e_k\notin\Delta_i\iff v+e_k\in U_{i-1}$, since $\alpha_i+(\beta+e_k)=v+e_k$. Thus these are the boundary lemma's two membership hypotheses, on the translated vector $v$. Apply [lem-trf-monotone-boundary-box] with the finite family $A=\{\alpha_h:h<i\}$. Its orthant union is $U_{i-1}$, monotone by Step 1; $M\ge1$, $|a|\le M$ for every $a\in A$, and $1\le k=r+1\le n$. Its witness $a=\alpha_h$ satisfies $a_k=v_k+1=\alpha_{i,k}+\beta_k+1$; its bound gives $v_j<M$ for $j\ge k$. Nonnegativity gives $\beta_j\le v_j<M$, the bound for $j>r$. For $i=1$, $A=\varnothing$ and $v+e_k\in U_0$ is impossible.

source.place: Agent coordinate proof of the quantitative exceptional-box refinement; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 (printed pp.93--94) gives only the parent resolution route. Compare Bierstone--Milman 1997, section 8, pp.273--275 (read online; absent from repository literature).

proof.text: For $i=0$ and $\beta\in E_{0,r}$, the complementary-region definition gives $\beta\notin D$ and $\beta+e_k\in D$. Apply [lem-trf-monotone-boundary-box] to $v=\beta$ and the finite family $A=\{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_s\}$. Its generated union equals $D$ by Step 1 and is monotone by hypothesis. Again $M\ge1$, every generator has total degree at most $M$, and $1\le k\le n$. Thus $\beta_j<M$ for every $j\ge k$, equivalently every $j>r$. The empty-family case has $D=\varnothing$ and admits no such entering vector.

source.place: Agent coordinate proof of the quantitative exceptional-box refinement; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 (printed pp.93--94) gives only the parent resolution route. Compare Bierstone--Milman 1997, section 8, pp.273--275 (read online; absent from repository literature).

proof.text: Every exceptional vector lies in $F_r$, so its first $r$ coordinates vanish. By Steps 2--3 its suffix $(\beta_{r+1},\ldots,\beta_n)$ belongs to $\{0,\ldots,M-1\}^{n-r}$. This suffix determines the vector uniquely since the omitted coordinates are zero. Conversely, extending any such suffix by $r$ zeros gives a vector in the containing box. The box thus has $M^{n-r}$ elements, proving the inclusion and finiteness. If $D=\varnothing$, then $\Delta_0=\mathbf N^n$ and there are no exceptions. If $D=\mathbf N^n$, the sole vertex is $0$, $\Delta_1=\mathbf N^n$ and $\Delta_0=\varnothing$, again giving none. When $n=1$ or $r=n-1$, $k=n$ and the boundary lemma bounds the sole surviving coordinate.

lean.statement: theorem faceExceptions_subset_box_and_finite {n s : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) (D : Set (Fin n →₀ ℕ)) (hD : IsMonotone D) (α : Fin s → Fin n →₀ ℕ) (hα : IsOrderedVertexFamily D α) (i : Option (Fin s)) (r : Fin n) : faceExceptions D α i r ⊆ {β | (∀ j : Fin n, j < r → β j = 0) ∧ ∀ j : Fin n, r ≤ j → β j < vertexDegreeBound α} ∧ (faceExceptions D α i r).Finite
